title.narrative: One UN Human Rights in the Transnistrian region 2022-2025
One UN Human Rights in the Transnistrian region 2022-2025

description.narrative:
Output 1. Increased capacities of vulnerable right holders to exercise their human rights
Objective 1.1. Enhanced human rights skills and knowledge of vulnerable rights holders Objective 1.2. Strengthened institutional capacity of partner CSOs and informal groups Objective 1.3. Improved service delivery of CSOs
The programme will continue providing support in developing the human rights knowledge of vulnerable groups and their CSOs in order to enhance their expertise on specific relevant human rights issues and related services (Roma mediators, sexual reproductive health for youth, gender sensitive services for women who use drugs, trust line for domestic and trafficking victims, referral and social reintegration for former prisoners, HIV, TB and drug dependency services for prisoners), but also on general ones such as discrimination, gender equality, and applying HRBA. As well, an institutional capacity building program will continue for CSOs and CBOs in order to strengthen their sustainability and create synergies between the civil society organizations on the left bank. By these interventions, the programme intends to enable and sustain CSOs to provide accessible, available, acceptable, and quality services (including online) for their beneficiaries, applying the good practices shared by CSOs from the right bank of Nistru. The final goal of the outcome is to pilot the transfer of build-up services to the local de facto structures, ensuring their sustainability, but also shaping an augmented engagement between CSOs and LPSs.
The cross-river cooperation between the CSOs from both banks will be further supported via sharing and learning (joint grants, study visits, transfer of knowledge, mentoring and coaching). The Platform for Sustainable Community Development (of 39 CSOs and initiative groups from both banks of the Nistru river working with various vulnerable groups) will be supported via its Secretariat and thematic groups to advocate for social changes.
Output 2. Improved systems and mechanisms for the respect, protection and fulfilment of human rights of vulnerable groups
Objective 2.1. Enhanced human rights compliant regulatory framework Objective 2.2. Improved existing service delivery systems
The output 2 foresees to continue to support the establishment of human rights mechanisms in the Transnistrian region based on recommendations produced by UN Human Rights mechanisms. Increased participation of CSOs in decision making and their capacity in advocating for inclusive services for the most vulnerable ones is considered a priority principle for this effort. The programme will support inclusive and meaningful participation of CSOs in the following processes: 1. drafting and implementation of the regional Human Rights Framework (a document that translates 137 recommendations from UN HR monitoring mechanisms and Thomas Hammerberg Report in relation to TN region); 2. monitoring the regional HIV regulations adjusted within previous phase; 3. promote and implement the regional Road map for child rights in the Transnistrian region (currently in the draft status); 4. the implementation of SOPs development for Makarenko school; 5. the development of a regional post release programme (including for children in custody in Alexandrovca penitentiary) and the implementation of training programme for professionals working with children in contact with the law; 6. development of regional child-friendly procedures for victims of violence including victims of crimes (Barnhaus type services); 7. implementation of referral services of PWUD and PLWH to harm reduction via cooperation between police structures and CSOs.
Output 3. Enhanced human rights culture in the Transnistrian region
Objective 3.1. Enhanced human rights capacity of the media Objective 3.2. Raised human rights awareness
The programme intends to continue to build capacity of media including bloggers and journalism students from both banks on the rights of vulnerable groups including via "HR Media Academy" (rights of people with disabilities and children's rights). Additionally, awareness raising campaigns around international human rights related days (social media, TV) will be further supported. The intervention will renew the existent comprehensive road map on PLWH de-stigmatization and will support its implementation with the focus on people leaving with HIV (empowering men and women leaving with HIV via mentoring programme); health staff (curriculas in medical schools will be revised to mainstream human rights; trainings will be provided); general public (via awareness campaigns).

Output 1. increased capacities of vulnerable right-holders to exercise their human rights the Programme is expected to achieve the following results: enhanced human rights skills and knowledge of vulnerable rights holders, strengthened institutional capacity of CSOs and informal groups, and improved service delivery of CSOs; under Output 2. improved systems and mechanisms for the respect, protection and fulfilment of human rights of vulnerable groups - enhanced human rights compliant regulatory framework, strengthened human rights institutions and improved service delivery as a result of advocacy actions from CSOs and human rights defenders; and under Output 3. enhanced human rights culture in the Transnistrian region - enhanced human rights capacity of the media and raised human rights awareness.

Resultat 1. Ökad kapacitet hos utsatta rättighetsinnehavare att utöva sina mänskliga rättigheter Programmet förväntas uppnå följande resultat: förbättrade mänskliga rättigheters färdigheter och kunskap om utsatta rättighetsinnehavare, stärkt institutionell kapacitet hos civila organisationer och informella grupper, och förbättrad serviceleverans av CSOs; under Output 2. Förbättrade system och mekanismer för respekt, skydd och uppfyllelse av mänskliga rättigheter för utsatta grupper - förbättrat regelverk som överensstämmer med mänskliga rättigheter, stärkta institutioner för mänskliga rättigheter och förbättrad serviceleverans som ett resultat av förespråkande åtgärder från civila organisationer och människorättsförsvarare; och under resultat 3. Förbättrad kultur för mänskliga rättigheter i Transnistrien-regionen - förbättrad medias kapacitet för mänskliga rättigheter och ökad medvetenhet om mänskliga rättigheter.

Programme activities were affected by security concerns on both sides of the Nistru River due to the volatile geopolitical situation, specifically the conflict in Ukraine. This added a new dimension to the Programme's activities, primarily carried out online,which adversely affected interaction with partners and beneficiaries. However, when situation permitted, face-to-face activities were organized, fostering closer relations and cooperation between CSO leaders and human rights activists from both banks. It has to be mentioned that the security concerns forced some of the staff of the Programme to be more reluctant to travel to the region, while some of the local CSOs partners reduced their activity or left the region. Also, some delays in the implementation of the One UN JA activities were caused by the newly introduced internal procurement system. The interaction with the Sustainable (Community) Development Platform (SCDP) was reactivated, expanding its membership and outlining future activities. An important change was the reduction of Thematic Working Groups number from three to two due to overlapping membership and complementary activities of the Adjustment of the Normative Framework and Advocacy groups. The awareness of the members of the Sustainable (Community) Development Platforms members was raised in the area of human-rights-compliant community-based services, by organising a roundtable in Tiraspol on Human Rights and Social Services with the participants from both banks of the Nistru River. From mid-2023, the trust line for the victims of gender-based violence in the Transnistrian region was supported, receiving 306 domestic violence-related calls and managing 18 SOS cases for women. In the same area guidelines for sexual violence support were developed and presented during a workshop. IOM also provided burnout prevention training to NGO staff in December due to increased workload from the Ukraine war, improving their ability to assist those in need and collaborate effectively. Work with CSOs, working or representing the PLHIV continued in the Phase II of the One UN JA. Key activities included organizing training sessions for their staff and beneficiaries to deepen the understanding of CLM principles and identifying critical areas for improvement in HIVrelated services and human rights. A targeted questionnaire was developed to assess awareness among PLHIV, revealing ongoing challenges in disclosure, employment, and testing procedures.
The Programme actively supported human rights defenders and activists in the Transnistrian region through various initiatives. Key activities included capacity-building for disability rights, creating a cross-river referral pathway for refugees with disabilities, and strengthening partnerships to aid Roma communities in obtaining identification documents. To improve service delivery of CSOs, the Programme supported the institutionalization of the Roma community mediators network in the Transnistrian region. This included consultations, renewing support through the Roma CSO Shatior over Nistru, and facilitating access to various services for both local Roma and Roma refugees from Ukraine. Cross-river cooperation with mediators from the right bank of the Nistru River was strengthened, and the network received positive feedback at a national forum. Additionally, Shatior over Nistru underwent a PSEA assessment to enhance its capacity and align with UN standards, with ongoing support planned for the next year. The three Crisis Rooms were established to provide temporary shelter and support for women who use drugs (WUD) and their children, facing domestic violence. These rooms also accommodated refugee women and children from Ukraine. Consultations were carried over to transfer this service to local administration. To ensure the continuation of the efforts initialised in the first phase of the Programme, in close cooperation with the Ministry of Justice an Informative Note on community reintegration for people released from detention in Moldova was finalised and disseminated. This document outlines six key interventions: family support, housing and financial assistance, health and social services access, substance abuse and behaviour change programmes, job placement assistance, and monitoring of ex-prisoners. A new element was introduced in the Phase II of the One UN JA - work with young people on sexual and reproductive health. An out-of-school comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) programme for 60 young people from the Transnistrian region was developed and implemented. This initiative addresses misinformation and promotes informed decisions about sexual and reproductive health and involved young people from various vulnerable backgrounds. Feedback indicates increased awareness and confidence among participants. Additionally, a Facilitators Manual was translated into Russian to support the programme. Additionally, 10 CSOs working with young people have been empowered and increased their capacity to integrate CSE in their programmatic activity and promote healthier behaviours and relationships. To enhance CSOs advocacy actions, the Programme facilitated the development of a Human Rights Framework (HRF) with the participation of local CSOs and human rights defenders. The draft HRF, consulted with de facto structures, is under consideration and will be finalized in early 2024. Concurrently, CSOs from both sides of the Nistru River contributed to creating a new human rights framework for Moldova, addressing specific issues in the Transnistrian region. Additionally, new human rights education curricula were introduced in collaboration with the State University of Medicine and Pharmacy to combat stigma and discrimination among future medical professionals. Four training sessions were held for doctors and nurses in Tiraspol and Ungheni, enhancing their communication skills and promoting non-discriminatory practices, as highlighted by the Stigma Index 2022. This initiative underscored the commitment to improving medical services and respecting patient rights, particularly for those affected by HIV. A significant step in bridging healthcare initiatives and fostering inclusivity in the region has been successfully implemented through a collaborative initiative aimed at empowering 149 doctors and nurses from both banks of the Nistru River with the essential skills and knowledge to cultivate a supportive and non-discriminatory environment for individuals affected by HIV. The Roadmap for Child Rights in the Transnistrian region, developed during the previous phase of the One UN JA and validated by de facto structures, faces challenges in its approval and implementation. Despite participatory development and validation by the de facto structures, the Programme still face challenges. The implementation of the Roadmap requires significant amendments to the de facto normative framework, shifting towards gender-sensitive and childfriendly justice, which will impact front-line workers and justice sector professionals. Additional advocacy efforts, including roundtable discussions, capacity-building initiatives, and empowerment activities for CSOs, are planned. The child rights curriculum is being used in three universities in the region, with public lectures and capacity-building activities for both preservice and in-service professionals underway. Advocacy efforts supported by the One UN JA, included participation in the 16 Days of Activism campaign, raised awareness of domestic violence issues. Awareness sessions on gender-based violence were conducted for Roma women, with plans to continue these efforts in 2024. In the second phase of the Programme substantial progress was made in enhancing the environment for people living with HIV (PLHIV) on the left bank of the Nistru River. Building on previous policy changes, the project focused on community-led monitoring (CLM) to ensure these changes were effectively implemented. The Programme continued its work with media, by organising human rights media brunches to build the capacity of media representatives from both banks of the Nistru River. These events, attended by over 25 journalists and media professionals, covered topics such as the access of Ukrainian refugees with disabilities to healthcare and the human rights of older persons. Through these sessions, media representatives gained deeper insights into the challenges faced by marginalized groups and the importance of adopting a human rights-based approach in their reporting. The Programme supported human rights awareness-raising initiatives in the Transnistrian region to promote the rights of marginalized groups. Key activities included public events on human-rights-compliant community-based services, on temporary protection status for Ukrainian refugees, an awareness event celebrating Roma rights, various campaign on HIV awareness and combating related stigma and a project creating human rights murals to symbolize social cohesion. These initiatives significantly enhanced knowledge and engagement on human rights issues among diverse communities.
Additionally, the mentoring programme, successfully launched in the first phase of the One UN JA, trained 36 women and 5 men in psycho-social skills and rights, empowering them to live free from stigma and violence. Monthly sessions on mental health, co-dependency, and overcoming violence created impactful experiences, exemplified by testimonials like Linda Anataciuc's.
Update 2023: In January 2023, the programme set out on an ambitious journey to strengthen security sector governance in Moldova under the "Strengthening Security Sector Governance in Moldova" (SSGM) Programme. Jointly implemented by a consortium of UN agenciesincluding IOM, OHCHR, UNAIDS, UNICEF, UNFPA, UNDP, and UNODCand coordinated by UNDP with Alexandru Stratulat at the helm, the initiative quickly established a comprehensive roadmap for change.
At the outset, the programme sought to create a more streamlined and effective approach. The Sustainable (Community) Development Platform (SCDP) was reactivated, and the number of Thematic Working Groups was reduced from three to two, a move that was designed to simplify coordination and enhance collaborative efforts. A roundtable in Tiraspol further bolstered these efforts by raising awareness about the importance of human rights-compliant community services.
The anticipated achievements soon began to materialize. Training sessions were organized to help NGO staff manage the increased workload and prevent burnoutan issue exacerbated by the ongoing Ukraine conflict. At the same time, capacity-building initiatives were launched for civil society organizations (CSOs) working with people living with HIV, pinpointing key areas for improving HIV services. The programme also extended its support to human rights defenders by offering specialized training in disability rights and establishing referral pathways for refugees with disabilities. Efforts to support vulnerable groups reached out to the Roma community through targeted consultations and cross-river cooperation, while temporary shelters and support services were provided for women who use drugs, as well as refugee women and children from Ukraine.
In a notable innovation, the programme introduced a new component focused on sexual and reproductive health education for young people in the Transnistrian region. This was complemented by the development of a Human Rights Framework (HRF) and the launch of new human rights education curricula aimed at combating stigma and discrimination among future medical professionals. Additional initiatives, such as media brunches and awareness-raising events, further amplified the impact by empowering communities with essential psychosocial skills and a robust understanding of their rights.
The volatile geopolitical situationmarked by the conflict in Ukrainecreated significant security concerns that hampered face-to-face interactions. Many activities had to be moved online, leading to a reduction in direct support and engagement with beneficiaries. The introduction of a new internal procurement system also caused delays, particularly affecting the implementation of One UN JA activities. Furthermore, overlapping roles between the Adjustment of the Normative Framework and Advocacy groups necessitated structural changes, and the Roadmap for Child Rights in the Transnistrian region, despite validation by de facto structures, struggled to gain approval due to the need for extensive amendments to existing regulations.
Despite these unexpected hurdles, the programme demonstrated a remarkable capacity for adaptation. Its flexible approach allowed it to navigate security concerns and operational limitations, ensuring that progress continued even under challenging circumstances. In the end, both the expected outcomes and the unforeseen challenges collectively underscored the programmes resilience and commitment to promoting human rights, community development, and effective governance in Moldova.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
